title.narrative: Chongqing Urban Rural Integration Project II-Health

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to improve the access of populations in selected non-metropolitan areas to County/District level hospital-based services, raising the efficiency of service production and improving the quality of care in targeted hospitals.

The development objective of the Second Health Chongqing Urban-Rural Integration Project is to improve the access of populations in selected non-metropolitan areas to county/district level hospital-based services, raising the efficiency of service production and improving the quality of care in targeted hospitals. The project comprises two components: the first component of the project is strengthening service delivery performance. This component comprises four sub-components which will support specific non- infrastructure aspects to complement the construction of county/district level hospitals. The second component of the project is improvement of county/district level health facilities. This component comprises two sub-components which will support the construction of new facilities in the eight selected counties/districts including hospital compound, inpatient building, outpatient service building, and medical technology building. These components have been designed to support the objective of improving access of populations in selected non-metropolitan areas to county/district level hospital-based services, raising the efficiency of service production and improving the quality of care in the targeted hospitals, which broadly support urban and rural integrated development in Chongqing.

comment.narrative: <p>133 percent achieved. This indicator measures the cumulative number of health personnel receiving training through this project.This is a core sector indicators and need to report the actual number every year. The end target was not set until the first restructuring. The end target was firstly achieved in December 2018 (as per ISR NO.14) and further increased to 1863 (as per final ISR).</p>

title.narrative: Number of high volume inpatient conditions or diseases treated using clinical pathways in project hospitals.

comment.narrative: <p>120 percent achieved. The indicator tracks the quality improvement of service delivery in project hospital. The original target was 10 diseases/conditions using clinical pathway accounting for 15 percent of the total admission. Since the project was extended three years in the first restructuring, the end target was revised to set a higher standard comparing to the original one according to the implementation status and plan at the time of the restructuring. In addition, the measure on the proportion of the admissions using clinical pathways was dropped. The target was firstly achieved in June 2018 (as per ISR NO.13) and further improved to 20 (as per final ISR).</p>

title.narrative: Number of project hospitals with a cooling system that meets national standard (GB19577, GB19576, GB21454 and GB 29540) on energy consumption cap and energy efficiency category

comment.narrative: <p>Successfully achieved. This indicator is core sector indicator. The construction has been delayed, in particular before the mid-term review. The end target was revised in the third restructuring to reflect the change of scope (two hospitals would be funded by domestic resources). The end target was firstly achieved in October 2020 (as per ISR NO.18). The result was confirmed in the final ISR.</p>

title.narrative: Number of evaluations conducted on pre-reform packages

comment.narrative: <p>Overachieved for 6 times of the revised end target. This indicators measures the progress in capacity building on project management and impact evaluation. The end target was reduced in the first restructuring as the evaluation planned to be conducted only at the last year of the project. Nevertheless, the PMO decided to launch evaluations in 2018 for the activities that had been implemented. The target was firstly achieved in June 2018 (as per ISR NO.13) and further increased to 6 (as per final ISR).</p>

title.narrative: Number of project hospital buildings that meet or exceed the National Energy Saving Standard

comment.narrative: <p>Successfully achieved. This indicator measures the progress in implementing energy efficient standard in hospital construction. The end target was revised in the third restructuring to reflect the change of scope (two hospitals would be funded by domestic resources). The end target was firstly achieved in October 2020 (as per ISR NO.18). The result was confirmed in the final ISR.</p>

title.narrative: Health facilities constructed, renovated, and/or equipped (number)

comment.narrative: <p>The indicator was dropped as it measured process rather than output/outcome. In addition, completing 60 percent of the annual plan was not sufficient to deliver the planned project by the new closing date.</p>

title.narrative: Number of Community Health Centers and Township Health Centers having signed coordination and referral agreements with each project/county hospital implementing coordinated care package

comment.narrative: <p>233 percent achieved. The indicator tracks progress on coordination of care among facilities at different levels. Since the project was extended three years in the first restructuring, the end target was revised to set a higher standard comparing to the original one. Still, the revised end target appeared to be underestimated. The target was firstly achieved in June 2018 (as per ISR NO.13) and further improved substantially to 98 (as per final ISR).</p>

title.narrative: Average length of stay in project hospitals

comment.narrative: <p>106.25 percent achieved. The indicator measure the efficiency improvement of project hospitals by tracking the reduction of the average number of days admission in the project hospital. Since the project was extended three years in the first restructuring, theend target was revised to set a higher standard comparing to the original one. The indicator was firstly achieved in July 2019 (as per ISR NO.15) and further improved to 7.5 percent in January 2021 (as per final ISR).</p>

title.narrative: Percent of inpatient referred to upper level hospitals, disaggregated by gender

comment.narrative: <p>112 percent achieved. The indicator tracks the improvement of service delivery capacity of project hospitals. At the approval, the indicator was no disaggregate by gender; it was revised to have sub-indicator for female and male in the first restructuring. Meanwhile, since the project was extended for three years, the end target was revised to set a higher standard comparing to the original one. The indicator was firstly achieved in July 2019 (as per ISR NO.15) and further improved to 4.4 percent in January 2021 (as per final ISR).</p>
